The MPON sents the dismissal to the MPOO.

args.text: When the description explicitly says that one participant sends information or an item to another participant, model the sending action as a Send Task rather than a generic Task.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already addresses the choice between a generic task and a Send Task for an explicitly described sending action.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.

args.text: When the description explicitly states that an activity sends information or an item to another participant, model it as a Send Task rather than a generic Task.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the send-task distinction.

result.rule: When the description states that one participant sends information to another participant: Model and label the activity from the sender’s perspective as sending the information, rather than as the recipient receiving it.

When the description states that an activity evaluates information and communicates a resulting outcome to another participant: Label the corresponding task to preserve both the evaluation and the communication, rather than naming only the communication.
When the description states that a person must supply or enter information: Model that human-performed activity as a user task rather than as a generic task.

When the description says that an outside participant performs work of its own or returns information after receiving input, rather than merely naming that participant as a recipient or source: Model that participant as a separate pool and represent the described exchanges with message flows between valid interaction nodes; keep the initiating participant’s work in its own pool.
